| `ARM7M-START-001` — Maps two separate device-memory regions from the provider (mapDeviceMemoryWithIndex(0) and (1), same vtable slot +0x208), storing the IOMemoryMap objects at this+0x54 and this+0x5c, then caches each one's virtual address (vtable+0x4c, getVirtualAddress()) at this+0x58 and this+0x60 respectively. Both this+0x58 and this+0x60 are passed together to the same "mapped I/O registers" log call. | `AppleARM7M::start(IOService*)` | disassembly | [docs/research/2026-10-16-wifi-iop-architecture.md#the-missing-producer-everything-checked-for-the-real-sdhc-base-pointer](2026-10-16-wifi-iop-architecture.md#the-missing-producer-everything-checked-for-the-real-sdhc-base-pointer) |
| `ARM7M-START-002` — this+0x50 holds the cached provider (AppleARMIODevice*). | `AppleARM7M::start(IOService*)` | disassembly | [tools/iop_analysis/appleARM7M_notes.md](https://github.com/SebE585/trognon/blob/main/tools/iop_analysis/appleARM7M_notes.md) |
| `ARM7M-STARTCPU-001` — Real entry point located at 0x80713664 (Thumb pointer 0x80713665), confirmed via its own "segLength >= md->getLength()" / AppleARM7M.cpp:155 REQUIRE string reference -- distinct from the pure-virtual-call trap stub at 0x80713e80, which only loads the signature string's address. | `AppleARM7M::startCPU(IOSlaveFirmware*)` | disassembly | [tools/iop_analysis/appleARM7M_notes.md](https://github.com/SebE585/trognon/blob/main/tools/iop_analysis/appleARM7M_notes.md) |
| `ARM7M-STARTCPU-002` — Programs the index-0 register window (this+0x58) with, in this order: +0x100 <- 0x10; a readback of +0x100 tested for bit 1; +0x118 <- the constant 0x86300000; +0x110 <- the value stored at this+0x88 (result of an md vtable call, ARM7M-STARTCPU-Q5); +0x114 <- a size field (ARM7M-STARTCPU-004); finally +0x100 <- 1. CORRECTED 2026-10-16: the earlier wording ("the firmware's raw bytes/length" written to +0x110/+0x114/+0x118) was wrong -- +0x118 is a literal constant, not firmware data, and no firmware bytes are written by this function. | `AppleARM7M::startCPU(IOSlaveFirmware*)` | disassembly | [tools/iop_analysis/appleARM7M_notes.md](https://github.com/SebE585/trognon/blob/main/tools/iop_analysis/appleARM7M_notes.md) |
| `ARM7M-STARTCPU-003` — Entry guard: takes the lock object at this+0x7c, then tests the byte at this+0x80. If non-zero, no hardware register is touched and the function returns 0xe00002d5 after releasing the lock. The byte is set to 1 only on the success path, right after the +0x100 <- 1 write. | `AppleARM7M::startCPU(IOSlaveFirmware*)` | disassembly | [tools/iop_analysis/appleARM7M_notes.md](https://github.com/SebE585/trognon/blob/main/tools/iop_analysis/appleARM7M_notes.md) |
| `ARM7M-STARTCPU-004` — The firmware length returned by the md vtable call at +0x84 is checked against segLength (REQUIRE, line 155). The size field at this+0x8c is the smallest power of two that is >= max(0x1000, length) (a doubling loop starting at 0x1000). If this+0x64 (the iop-version property, value 1 on this device) equals 1, +0x114 receives (-size) & 0x3ffff000; otherwise it receives size unchanged. | `AppleARM7M::startCPU(IOSlaveFirmware*)` | disassembly | [tools/iop_analysis/appleARM7M_notes.md](https://github.com/SebE585/trognon/blob/main/tools/iop_analysis/appleARM7M_notes.md) |
| `ARM7M-STARTCPU-005` — Ordering: the write of 1 to window0+0x100 is the last register write of the function, followed by one provider vtable call (+0x220), the unlock, and a return of 0. Nothing after that write waits for, or reads back, any IOP state within this function. | `AppleARM7M::startCPU(IOSlaveFirmware*)` | disassembly | [tools/iop_analysis/appleARM7M_notes.md](https://github.com/SebE585/trognon/blob/main/tools/iop_analysis/appleARM7M_notes.md) |
| `ARM7M-VIC-001` — A method (statically referenced from a vtable slot at 0x807143f0 -- proof of a code reference pointing at it, not proof that this slot is ever called at runtime) takes one integer argument (0 or 1) and writes a 32-bit word -- 8 if arg==0, 4 if arg==1 -- to [this+0x60 + 0x18], i.e. to offset +0x18 of the window this project calls SOC_IOP_VIC_BASE (0xBF300000). Guarded by a call through this+0x7c both on entry and before returning (plausibly a lock). | `vic_write_0x18 (working name, not Apple's)` | disassembly | [tools/iop_analysis/appleARM7M_notes.md](https://github.com/SebE585/trognon/blob/main/tools/iop_analysis/appleARM7M_notes.md) |
| `IOSLAVE-INIT-001` — This kext's module-load code registers six OSMetaClass instances -- IOSlaveMemory (8), IOSlaveMemoryBuffer (16), IOSlaveEndpoint (56), IOSlaveCPU (80), IOSlaveFirmware (80), IOSlaveProcessor (104) bytes -- each size read as a literal loaded right before the shared OSMetaClass constructor call. | `module init (OSMetaClass registration loop)` | disassembly | [tools/iop_analysis/appleARM7M_notes.md](https://github.com/SebE585/trognon/blob/main/tools/iop_analysis/appleARM7M_notes.md) |
| `IOSLAVE-INIT-002` — No loading/firmware logic found within the reviewed_ranges above (the init loop and the six constructor-call sites, ~230 of this kext's 2968 __text bytes). This does NOT cover the kext's other functions seen in the function list but not individually read (0x80399848, 0x803998c0, 0x803998d8, 0x80399900 -- 120 bytes, role unknown) -- the claim is bounded to what was actually read, not the whole binary. | `module init (OSMetaClass registration loop)` | disassembly | [tools/iop_analysis/appleARM7M_notes.md](https://github.com/SebE585/trognon/blob/main/tools/iop_analysis/appleARM7M_notes.md) |
